clue.text: Bearded old party leader sat for artist

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

parts.note: the first letter of party
a model sits, or poses, for a painter

explanation.surface: A bearded elderly political chief once sat for his portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearded' looks like a description of the old leader, but it is the definition: to beard someone is to confront them boldly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beard someone means to defy or confront them face to face, so bearded works as a past-tense verb for resisted.

clue.text: He speaks of sports centre on a hill

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the innermost pair of letters is kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of sports
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone giving a talk about a leisure complex built on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker, especially a skilled and eloquent one, is defined simply as a man who speaks.

clue.text: Meets the cost of fight by telephone

parts.note: to pay is to meet the cost
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone covering the expense of a boxing match arranged over the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated public phone kiosk can be called by this compound, so it stands for a telephone.

clue.text: What the sick may resort to

definitions.text: What the sick may resort to

parts.note: surface reading: what ill people may fall back on as a last measure
setter's reading: a health resort where invalids go to recover

explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort to' reads as a verb phrase meaning turn to, but the answer is a resort in the holiday sense, a place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an establishment, often in the hills or by the sea, where invalids and convalescents stay to rest and recover.

clue.text: Cook lived up to his name

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef who earned the reputation his name promised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a person or Captain Cook, but it is a verb: to cook food with hot spices.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook food such as kidneys with a hot spicy seasoning is a classic kitchen verb.

clue.text: Aerial missile or a submarine hazard

parts.note: a bomb is dropped from the air
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between a bomb from above and something lurking under the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A bombora is an Australian word for a submerged reef or rock over which waves break; 'submarine' here means underwater, not the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians use this word for a hidden offshore reef that endangers boats, a genuine danger lying beneath the surface.

clue.text: City where East European had one extra

parts.note: a Balt comes from Latvia, Lithuania or Estonia
I is the Roman numeral for one
more means additional

explanation.surface: A town where a visitor from the Baltic received a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large port in the American state of Maryland, an example of a city.

clue.text: Kelly was a male, unknown

definitions.note: the definition is the adjective Kelly is described by

parts.note: a man is a male person
X is the classic unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A mysterious man called Kelly whose identity is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kelly from the Isle of Man' is an old British music-hall song, so Kelly came from that island.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine came from the Isle of Man, so she was of that island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Worn at the 12 by a bishop, perhaps

parts.note: a means one
a bishop is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Vestments worn at midday by a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 points to the lido entry, an open-air swimming pool, not a time. The answer is a one-piece swimsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming costume made in a single piece is what bathers wear at the open-air pool.

clue.text: Exhibit 'B' being gold and neon on the wing

parts.note: to air something is to put it on show
taken as written
or is gold in heraldry
Ne is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: A museum display of gold and neon items, labelled B, in a side wing of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wing' suggests a museum wing alongside the exhibit, but it means in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird on the wing is flying, and anything carried through the sky is likewise in flight.

clue.text: An Irishman was Hitler's favourite

parts.note: the indefinite article as a single letter
Ryan is a common Irish name

explanation.surface: An unlikely claim that some Irishman was the Nazi leader's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazi racial ideology held up the so-called master race of fair northern Europeans as the ideal people.

clue.text: An undertaker is found in this force

definitions.text: An undertaker is found in this force

parts.note: surface reading: a funeral director
setter's reading: someone who undertakes a task freely, serving in an unpaid reserve force

explanation.walkthrough: An undertaker here is simply one who undertakes, offering service of their own accord; the force is a reserve of unpaid soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who offers service willingly takes on a duty unasked, and such people made up the old citizen reserve units of the army.

clue.text: Daughter encircled by books about a gila could be a pain

indicators.note: something encircled sits inside a ring, so the books wrap around what comes before
could be suggests a possible rearrangement of the short phrase before it

parts.note: the Old Testament books of the Bible
taken as written, then rearranged
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A girl surrounded by books on a venomous lizard might find it a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The gila monster is a lizard, but 'a gila' is just five letters to rearrange into the Greek ending for pain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for toothache, from Greek odont- tooth and -algia pain, so it is one particular pain.

clue.text: Beginner speaking compliant words by the pool

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
the words of agreement said at a wedding

explanation.surface: A newcomer saying yes to everything beside the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names a public open-air swimming pool or bathing place, so it stands for the pool itself.

clue.text: Cambrian contralto or soldier seen with the Queen

parts.note: Cambria is the Latin name for Wales
C is a common abbreviation for contralto
taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A Welsh singer or a soldier spotted in the company of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth II was famous for her pet short-legged herding dogs of this Welsh breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The late Queen kept dozens of these little dogs, which constantly accompanied her in photographs.

clue.text: It transmits 10 in a core band, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters given are only one possible order of them

parts.note: the digits one and zero written as letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something broadcasting a number inside the central group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but here it is just the digits, read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigation device sends out a constant signal that ships and aircraft use to fix their position, so it transmits.

clue.text: One in three-D version: King Stephen, say

indicators.note: in here only places the word before alongside the scrambled letters
a version is a different rendering, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: the word as printed less one of its two Es, which the parse has no use for: the setter's slip
taken as written
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A 3-D remake of a story about the medieval English king.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, three-D supplies a spare E; the parse works with just one. Stephen seized the English throne in 1135 from Matilda, Henry I's chosen heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen took the crown meant for his cousin Matilda, so he is an example of someone who removes a ruler from the throne.

clue.text: Kit Carson''s vehicle?

parts.note: surface reading: the Wild West frontiersman
setter's reading: a vehicle belonging to a man employed as an army scout, or a military reconnaissance vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: Kit Carson was a famous US Army scout in the American West, so his transport would be a military reconnaissance vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured reconnaissance vehicle is named for the scouting job it does, which was exactly Carson's job.

clue.text: Marks half inside one gain accidentally

indicators.note: half means only the front portion of the word after it survives

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something done accidentally falls out in a random, unplanned order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A student scoring half marks by luck on an inside question.
explanation.definitionFit: Badges or emblems of rank and office are distinguishing marks worn to show status.

clue.text: She leads against Custer's 500, perhaps

parts.note: con as in pros and cons, the case against

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters before it are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A woman commanding the fight against General Custer's forces.
explanation.walkthrough: A conductress was the woman who took fares on a British bus; here the word is read as a woman who conducts, or leads.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct is to guide or lead, as an orchestra or a tour, and the feminine ending makes it a woman doing so.

clue.text: Meeting of opponents in choice setting

indicators.note: in places the first pair inside the word that follows
a setting holds a jewel, so this word wraps round the pair of letters

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one
East and North are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Rivals coming face to face in a chosen venue.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North partners South and East partners West, so North and East sit as opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A full assembly of all members of a body, such as a party committee, is this kind of meeting.

clue.text: Monty was killed by Apollo

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British comedy team's name, Monty ___
second meaning: the serpent of Delphi slain by the Greek god

explanation.walkthrough: Monty Python's Flying Circus was a British TV comedy series. In Greek myth Apollo shot the great serpent guarding Delphi.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedy troupe's surname completes Monty, and the Delphic dragon of myth was slain by the archer god.

clue.text: One being out of condition is disheartened

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: not physically fit

explanation.surface: Someone who has let their fitness slide feels downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thing considered as a whole is one item, so one being, a single entity, is described by this word.

clue.text: How ill was the reviewer?

parts.note: surface reading: asking how severe a sickness was
setter's reading: in the manner of a critic who reviews things

explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes both a dangerous level of illness and the fault-finding way a reviewer writes.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both gravely, of a patient near death, and in a judging, fault-finding way, like a critic.

clue.text: Cast appearing in "The Endless Column"

indicators.note: without an end, the word before loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a line of people or things one behind another

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors performing in a play with a grand title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a set of actors, but it is a verb meaning to fling.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a stone or a line is to fling or hurl it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: A follower, for example, holding royal composer

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet

indicators.note: holding means the abbreviation wraps around the next item

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for for example
R stands for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A devotee, for instance, attending a regal musician.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Alban Berg, the Austrian composer of Wozzeck.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was a twentieth-century Austrian writer of music, a pupil of Schoenberg.

clue.text: Legal offender

parts.note: surface reading: a lawbreaker of any kind
setter's reading: one who scorns the authority of a court

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the formal word for someone guilty of contempt, especially of court.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a person who shows contempt of court by disobeying or insulting it commits a specific legal offence.

clue.text: Where stock is managed by companion

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A place where goods are handled by a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests shop goods, but here it is livestock. CH is a British honour, the Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A large farm in the Americas where cattle or horses are raised is where livestock is kept.

clue.text: Mineral found in actual fish

parts.note: actual means real, genuine
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A rock discovered inside a genuine fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a red arsenic sulphide ore, one specific named mineral.

clue.text: He wrote "Western Assassin"

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west or western
a hired killer

explanation.surface: An author named as writer of a cowboy thriller about a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a book title, but the words are wordplay. The answer is the American poet Walt, of Leaves of Grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century American poet produced Leaves of Grass, so he is a man who wrote.
